title: Hard road trips with Earl Foster's band
summary: He recalls hungry road trips and a string of car breakdowns with Earl Foster's Cadillac, ending with his deciding to drive his own car and give up the road.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: That was tough. Stop on the road and eat watermelon. Anything you could see to eat. Corn, anything. Sugar cane, anything. That's true. Old bus break down and we walk. And I used to play with Earl Foster too. We used to play at Skinner's place out in Buccalus. Oh he had a Cadillac with crepe-de-sheen ties. Now he had to be there at work for nine o'clock and leave here at eight o'clock. Now he'd go across the bridge, you know how he lived? Like the tunnel over in the lake, the tie busted and all of them. Right on that whole bridge thing. Oh Jesus, it scared me from that. All right we get some slide there, we fix the tie, and we say, well Earl, you fix the tie so we're going to walk. You know, we get on the walk on the highway. We walk, we walk. So we walked on down there, about five or six acres, and some dogs, about a hundred dogs got behind us. I was leading the crowd. So Earl caught up with us down the road, and we got in the car and we all was holding, fingers crossed you know, and got up the road a little piece of the tie, let out again. Boom! I said, oh Lord, hold on. He said, don't worry, we're going to get there. I said, we're going to get out and walk some more. We got out and walk. He fixed the old car, got back in the car again. After he picked us up, I said, I guess we'll get there now and be riding back, sitting down there, whole crane and everything. So after a while you know, he got in the curve there and there come a horse cutting across the highway and he hit that horse. And there it was again, the horse went up there and come right back down on the windshield and rolled over the top and all of us was full of horsemen in there. Wow.
So I told him, I said. Were those open cars or something those days, or what were they like?
No, he had old hardtop Cadillac, one of them old miles.
Yeah, he had to pump it to make the fuel come up to it, you know.

Yeah, that's an old Cadillac you had. And them lights you couldn't see, they were old counter lights, like counter power lights. And I said I quit playing with her from that day, I said, if I go with him I'm going to take my own car, you see. And that's what I did, I'd take my car and make him pay me transportation to bring my car. I said, no, you take your men in the car, I'm going to go in my car. But them fellas they want to drink too, you know what I mean, see, and you can't drink and drive. No, I'm kidding.
Yeah, it's kind of tough on the road all right, you don't do that anymore Jim?
No, no, I don't do it anymore. I don't like the road no more.
